title: Tuning in
art_brief: Bumpy curled up holding one end of a paper tin-can telephone, its string looping out of the picture toward a few folded paper music notes, under a pale paper sky by day and a deep blue sky with paper stars by night.
bumpy_line: Hello out there! My ears are getting ready. Hum me something, any tune at all.

know.text: Around the end of this stretch, your baby starts to hear. In time they may pick up your heartbeat, the gurgles of your tummy and the voices close by.
know.source_title: 15 weeks pregnant guide - Best Start in Life - NHS

ready.text: Choose a song, rhyme or short story you like and keep it handy to share with your bump. Anyone close to you can join in. No voice is too off-key.
ready.suggested_question: What will happen at my next visit, and how can I reach you between visits if I have a question?

look_forward.text: Around now, some parents give their bump a nickname, and it can start to feel like a little someone. Bumpy thinks nicknames are a wonderful idea.

curious.question: What is my baby's brain busy building right now?

title: Middle of the map
art_brief: Bumpy sitting right at the centre fold of an open paper map, beside a tiny paper flag on a dotted path that runs from one edge of the map to the other, under a paper sun by day and a paper moon by night.
bumpy_line: Look at us, right in the middle of the map! I'm busy wiggling, napping and listening for you.

know.text: Around now, your baby moves around a lot and is settling into waking and sleeping times of their own. Their busy times may not match yours, and that is common.
know.source_title: 21 weeks pregnant guide - Best Start in Life - NHS

ready.text: Make a little rest corner: a cushion, a blanket, a glass of water and something to read. Somewhere to put your feet up for a moment.
ready.suggested_question: When might I start feeling my baby move, and who do I call if I'm ever unsure?

look_forward.text: Many parents first feel their baby move somewhere in this stretch, often like a soft flutter or bubble. In a first pregnancy it can come a little later.

curious.question: Why does my baby seem wide awake just when I want to sleep?

title: Making the nest
art_brief: Bumpy tucked into a round cut-paper bird's nest lined with paper leaves and a tiny folded paper blanket, resting on a paper branch, with a pale sky by day and a paper crescent moon and small glowing paper lantern by night.
bumpy_line: Getting snug in here! Tell me about home. Is it noisy, cozy, full of plants? I'm curious.

know.text: Your baby keeps moving right up to and during labour. If their usual pattern of movements ever changes, call your midwife, doctor or maternity unit straight away, even at night.

ready.text: Save the numbers for your doctor or midwife and your birth unit in your phone, and share them with someone close. Easy to find, any hour.
ready.suggested_question: Where do I go, and who do I call, when labour starts or if something feels different?

look_forward.text: Many parents start to picture the first hello around now. Daydream about it as much or as little as you like. Bumpy is daydreaming too.

curious.question: Are my baby's bones still getting stronger right now?
